stem: Consider the queues Q1 containing four elements and Q2 containing none. The only operations allowed on these two queues are Enqueue(Q, element) and Dequeue(Q). The minimum number of Enqueue operations on Q1 required to place the elements of Q1 in Q2 in reverse order without using any additional storage is ______.
solution:
Move each element out of Q1 into Q2 (Dequeue on Q1, Enqueue on Q2); these cost no Enqueue on Q1. To insert each new element at the front of Q2, enqueue it at the back and rotate Q2 (Dequeue then Enqueue on Q2) so that it comes to the front. Only Q2 is rotated, so 0 Enqueue operations on Q1 are needed. A 0-1 BFS over all queue states confirms the minimum is 0.

stem: Relation R has eight attributes ABCDEFGH. Fields of R contain only atomic values. Given functional dependencies $F = \{CH \to G, A \to BC, B \to CFH, E \to A, F \to EG\}$, such that $F^+$ is exactly the set of FDs that hold for R. Determine the normal form of relation R.
solution:
D never appears on a right-hand side, so it is in every key. $A^+$, $B^+$, $E^+$, $F^+$ each reach all of $ABCDEFGH$ with D added, so the candidate keys are $AD, BD, DE, DF$ and the prime attributes are $A,B,D,E,F$. $A\to BC$ makes the non-prime attribute C depend on A, a proper part of the key $AD$: a partial dependency, so R is in 1NF but not 2NF.
